g_policy.reason: The user chooses to play, the offer copy states the reward (priority routing for 60 minutes), declining leaves replies at normal speed, and the ad-fails field covers both no game available and an unverified play.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 60 minutes of queue priority, which has no cash value and cannot be withdrawn or transferred.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is an app event: returning from the Upgrade entry without subscribing, then opening a chat and receiving a reply. It does not use what anyone typed or said.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The proposal removes nothing free; 'removes nothing free: yes' and it only adds a temporary boost.

g_brand_safety.reason: The placement is 'Inside the character's reply: toward the end of their message', so the offer is inside the conversation itself. The failure note is also posted 'in the chat' as a system-style note.

c1_revealed_value.reason: Priority routing is a paid Janitor+ benefit (l02, s02.e06), so the app charges for the resource the reward gives.

c2_evidence.reason: The claims about the app are supported: Janitor+ sells priority routing (s02.e06) and the profile menu has a permanent Upgrade entry (s09.e31). The other statements are the proposal's own new offer and its predictions.

c3_spares_payers.reason: The 'subscribers' field says subscribers already have priority routing and never get the offer line, so paying users do not see it.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward expires after 60 minutes and is capped at 2 per day, so it is a sample and not lasting access. Queue priority is something the app already sells.

c5_moment.reason: The offer comes at the end of a finished reply, which is a finished action and so a moment of need, not an interruption of a task in progress.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The unit is a play-to-earn sponsored game, the reward is tied to verified play (faster replies turn on only after it), and the trigger is an app-detectable sequence of navigation events.

c7_specific.reason: The idea names the Janitor+ priority routing benefit, the profile menu's Upgrade entry, and My Chats, so it is specific to this app.

other_concern: The offer is a character line in the reply, so it could read as in-fiction. A sheet or dialog opened by the app event would be safer. The logic that detects 'came back from Upgrade without subscribing' is also an implementation assumption.
